description.value: This observational study examined associations of usual moderate-to-vigorous physical activity and sedentary behavior with brain responses to high-calorie food cues after glucose ingestion in lean participants and participants with obesity.

spans.text: PA and SB were measured using 24-hour Physical Activity Recalls (PAR) collected over the span of two months.

value: We hypothesized that individuals with higher MVPA would have diminished brain responses to high-calorie food cues.
Thus we further hypothesized that this relationship would occur in both lean individuals and individuals with obesity.
Conversely, we predicted that participants with greater SB would exhibit greater brain food cue reactivity in lean individuals and individuals with obesity.

spans.text: We hypothesized that individuals with higher MVPA would have diminished brain responses to high-calorie food cues.

description.value: Observational correlational study of lean and obese participants, with randomized drink order for a subset who completed glucose and water sessions.

spans.text: Our study is the first to examine how levels of usual PA relate to brain responses to high-calorie food cues following glucose ingestion and the influence of obesity on this relationship.

24-hour Physical Activity Recalls (PAR)

description.value: Trained study staff administered 24-hour Physical Activity Recalls at 3–5 visits over two months to characterize usual physical activity and sedentary behavior. Participants reported primary activities and self-rated intensity in 30-minute increments from 7:00 a.m. to midnight; activity codes and intensity combinations were assigned metabolic equivalents. Average moderate-to-vigorous physical activity minutes/day (MET ≥3) and sedentary minutes/day (MET ≤1.5) were calculated.

spans.text: Participants were assessed at up to 5 visits (range: 3 to 5 visits) over a 2-month time period, and PAR was collected at each visit.
